answers.answer: Keep 4 tokens of each gem color and all 5 gold tokens. Reveal 3 nobles; remove the other 7 permanently from the game.
answers.evidence: Token Setup Quick Reference: 2 players: 4 each, 5 gold, 3 nobles. Setup: 'Remove remaining noble tiles from the game'; Noble Tile Mechanics: 'out of the game permanently.'

answers.answer: Three players use 5 tokens per gem color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. Four players use 7 per gem color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more of each gem color and one more noble, with the same gold count.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count: 3 | 5 | 5 | 4; 4 | 7 | 5 | 5.

answers.answer: Shuffle each level separately. Arrange decks in a column with level 1 at the bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 at the top. Reveal 4 cards per level, 12 total. The youngest player starts and play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player: 'The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise.'

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 3 gems of different colors; take 2 gems of one color with at least 4 in its supply; reserve one card if holding fewer than 3 reserved cards and take gold if available; or buy one face-up or previously reserved card. Neither taking gems then buying nor reserving then buying that card is allowed on the same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of four actions; purchase option specifies 'reserved on a previous turn.'

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.'

answers.answer: You may take two green, leaving two, because the pile starts with four. You may not take two red from a pile of three. Check the threshold before taking the tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them'; Actions 1 and 2: 'You may not take gold tokens with this action.'

answers.answer: Temporarily holding 12 is allowed. Return 2 tokens to end with 10; these may include newly drawn gems. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'may temporarily exceed 10'; 'return tokens of their choice'; 'including gold'; 'may return some or all of the tokens they just took.'

answers.answer: Take the available gold, temporarily reaching 11 tokens, then return one token of your choice, possibly that gold, to end with 10. If gold is empty, you may still reserve and remain at 10 tokens without receiving gold.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold.' Token Hand Limit permits temporary excess and returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve a face-up market card or the top card of any of the three development decks. A card taken from a deck is not shown to opponents. Only the reserving player may buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'face-up development card'; 'top card from any one of the three level decks, without revealing it'; 'Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them.'

answers.answer: You cannot reserve with three reserved cards, even just to obtain gold. You cannot discard or exchange one to make room: purchase is the only way a reserved card leaves your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: 'If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another'; 'The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it.'

answers.answer: Immediately refill the level-2 space with the top card of the level-2 deck. Purchasing a face-up card uses the same replacement procedure. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy and requires no refill. If the relevant deck is empty, a market vacancy remains empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: 'Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced'; 'If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space in the grid remains empty for the rest of the game.'

answers.answer: Spend one green token and no blue tokens. If bonuses cover every required color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: the example says 'you only need to spend 1 green token'; 'without spending any tokens at all'; bonuses act as a 'permanent gem of that color.'

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses leave a cost of one blue, one black and one white. Pay the blue token for blue and the two gold for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Your purchased bonus cards stay with you.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce tokens needed; gold 'can substitute for any single gem token'; spent gems and gold return to supply. Bonus Stacking: each card adds a bonus 'permanently.'

answers.answer: Buy a face-up market card or one of your previously reserved cards. Place purchased cards face up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so their bonuses and prestige values remain visible to everyone at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card; 'sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible to all players at all times.'

answers.answer: You do not qualify with only two white bonuses; a white or gold token cannot fill the missing bonus. A third purchased white bonus makes you qualify at the end of your turn, subject to the one-noble limit. Having more bonuses than required is allowed.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: 'at least' the required bonuses; 'bonuses only ... not gem tokens'; Noble Tile Mechanics: 'having more is fine.'

answers.answer: Choose exactly one noble; you cannot take both or decline all visits. The other stays available. The visit is automatic, uses no action and grants 3 prestige. Check eligibility at the end of your turn after your action.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: 'cannot refuse it'; 'not an action'; 'choose one'; 'at most one noble per turn'; '3 prestige points.'

answers.answer: Place the noble tile face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.'

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns. A does not take another turn, since the round then ends with equal turn counts. B is not guaranteed to win; another player can finish with more prestige.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete the current round so all have the 'same number of turns'; End-of-Game Clarifications: the triggering player may lose if another 'surpasses them in the same final round.'

answers.answer: Your total becomes 16. This triggers the end condition because it is 15 or more. Complete the current round, then determine the winner by the final prestige totals.
answers.evidence: Nobles are worth 3; End-Game Trigger: '15 or more prestige points'; Determining the Winner: 'most prestige points at the end of the final round.'

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie on 16 prestige, and B has fewer purchased developments, 9 versus 10. C's lower prestige excludes C despite fewer cards. Noble points count. B's three unpurchased reserved cards do not count as purchased developments.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: 'most prestige points'; 'Noble tile points count'; Tiebreaker: 'fewest development cards' purchased. Prestige Point Sources specifies 'each purchased card.'

answers.answer: No. Unpurchased reserved cards contribute neither the eight points to scoring or the trigger nor the two white bonuses to discounts or noble requirements.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: 'Printed on each purchased card'; Payment rules: bonuses from 'previously purchased development cards'; Noble Visits: bonuses 'from purchased development cards.'

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased card gives a permanent blue discount for future purchases, and its blue bonus can satisfy a noble requirement even though the card scores zero prestige.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: bonuses 'never generate tokens'; each purchased card adds a bonus permanently. Noble Visits depends on bonuses from purchased cards, and card prestige 'may be 0.'

answers.answer: You cannot use that card's own bonus to buy it; with no blue bonus, blue token or gold you cannot pay. A newly purchased white bonus does count for a noble at the end of the same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: discounts come from 'previously purchased development cards'; Noble Visits checks bonuses from purchased cards 'At the end of their turn.'

answers.answer: The extra blue bonuses cannot cover green or produce blue tokens as change. You still owe two green tokens, with gold able to substitute for either or both.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess bonuses provide 'no benefit for that purchase (no "change" is given)'; bonuses reduce costs 'of that color'; gold substitutes for any gem token.

answers.answer: The first noble does not use up your permanent bonuses. Taking gems on your next turn can still lead to receiving the remaining noble at that turn's end, if it remains available. You cannot receive it during an opponent's intervening turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent. Noble Visits: others 'remain available for future turns'; eligibility is checked 'At the end of their turn'; at most one per turn.

answers.answer: Yes. You may reserve that face-up level-3 card with no tokens or developments; reserving does not require paying its printed purchase cost. Take one gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'Take one development card' from the grid or any deck, with only a three-card hand limit; 'also take 1 gold token.' Payment of printed cost appears under Purchase a Development Card.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled: all twelve remain. Take only that one top card into your hand; you do not take a second card as a replacement.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'Take one development card'; blind reservation takes the 'top card' from a level deck. Card replacement applies to a face-up card removed 'from the grid.'

answers.answer: The four face-up cards stay available for purchase or reservation. If one is purchased, its space remains empty for the rest of the game; the other three remain available.
answers.evidence: Purchase and Reserve allow face-up grid cards. Card Replacement: 'If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space in the grid remains empty for the rest of the game.'

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy the affordable reserved card or take one gem from each of three available colors. Continue until the normal prestige condition.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'Exhausting the development decks or the face-up market does not end the game. Continue with the remaining legal actions, including purchasing reserved cards.'

answers.answer: Yes. Temporarily take three different gems, then return all three newly taken tokens, ending with your original ten. No net gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'may temporarily exceed 10'; 'A player may return some or all of the tokens they just took.'

answers.answer: A returns the two spent gold to the supply; they are not removed from the game. B takes one when reserving, leaving one gold in the supply before token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'; Reserve a Development Card: take '1 gold token' if available.

answers.answer: You may purchase the level-3 face-up card now if you can pay for it. The purchase rules impose no lower-level prerequisite or unlocking requirement.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: 'Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card.'

answers.answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble visit. The purchase raises you to 15 and the noble raises you to 18. Players still due a turn in the current round continue playing before the game ends.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: 'automatic' and 'cannot refuse it'; noble worth 3. End-Game Trigger completes the current round for equal turn counts.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes that turn. A does not start another round and nobody gets another turn: A, B, C and D already have equal turn counts at the end of this round.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns.'

answers.answer: Do not reveal a replacement. The seven removed nobles are permanently out of play. Put the acquired noble face up in front of its recipient; two nobles remain available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Noble Tile Mechanics: removed nobles are 'out of the game permanently'; Noble visit rules: place received tile 'face-up in front of you.'

answers.answer: Emerald is green; diamond white; sapphire blue; onyx black; ruby red; gold joker yellow. There are 90 development cards: 40 level 1, 30 level 2 and 20 level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token table and Development Cards table: '90 total', Level 1 40, Level 2 30, Level 3 20.

answers.answer: You may spend gold instead and keep your green token. Return the spent gold to the supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: 'Gold tokens (jokers) can substitute for any single gem token. Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply.'

answers.answer: Yes, take one red, one blue and one green. The four-token minimum applies only to taking two of the same color. The piles then hold 0 red, 1 blue and 2 green.
answers.evidence: Action 1: 'Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles'; Action 2 alone specifies 'at least 4 tokens of that color.'

answers.answer: A direct gold-for-red exchange is not a listed action and is not authorized by the purchasing joker rule. Gold can substitute for a gem token when paying for a development card, after which it returns to the supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists exactly four actions; Gold Token Specifics: 'Gold tokens can substitute for any gem color when purchasing a card.'

answers.answer: You must choose one of the four actions. Voluntarily passing while legal actions are available is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'On their turn, a player must perform exactly one of the following four actions.'
